article.summary: Breadcrumbs is a public repository of coding-agent memory templates, hooks, scripts, and guardrails, rather than a hosted memory service. It places cues at session start, prompt lookup, file edits, and handoff, and includes two distinct file-backed examples: a TSV-indexed memory desk and a separate Python three-tier memory engine. This is source review, not runtime or benchmark evidence.

who_what.text: The official README frames Breadcrumbs as one person's working answer and says it is not a product or framework launch. The repository contains reusable templates, hooks, scripts and CI examples; the memory desk guide describes that desk as one part of a larger memory pattern. The reviewed code does not establish a hosted service or managed operator.

architecture.text: The top-level pattern places cues at existing work moments. The repository includes handoff, decisions, and settled-facts templates and hooks for session start, prompt lookup, and file edits. The examples are adopter-controlled artifacts, not one unified hosted store.

The memory desk stores settled facts in index.tsv with key, aliases, answer, source, and checked date; raw entries append to journal.jsonl. It also uses a small kernel file, tombstones.tsv, and review-only consolidation-proposals.jsonl. The desk is local to the repository where an adopter installs it.

A separate Python example defines working state in session_state.json, append-only events in episodes.jsonl, categorized facts in facts.json, and rejected values in tombstones.json. It assumes a caller-owned agent loop and is not the memory-desk CLI or data store.

behavior.text: The desk's mem add appends a timestamped capture; a later gardener pass promotes durable facts to the TSV index. The separate engine exposes set_goal, note, log_episode, and store_fact. These are code-visible write paths, not an assertion that the repository is deployed with them.

For the desk, gardener promotion updates an exact key collision; semantic duplicates become review proposals. mem reject removes a matching active row, records a dated tombstone with a reason, and journals the correction; mem check refuses the same key/value if it returns. recheck detects changed source files but does not judge truth. Engine overwrites log a SUPERSEDED episode, and a changed value begins asserted; writing the same value preserves its status.

Retirement is not physical erasure in the reviewed paths: desk journal entries remain append-only and tombstones retain rejected values. Engine reject_fact removes the active fact but records the value in a tombstone and REJECTED episode; lifting a tombstone also appends an event. No general physical-erasure API was found in the inspected paths.

Desk lookup checks exact keys and aliases before token-overlap ranking and returns at most three rows. Its prompt hook reads at most 400 characters and filters weak matches; the session-start hook emits the kernel, up to three recent journal lines, and row count. A desk miss prints a search-and-capture ladder. Engine build_context combines working data, eligible facts, and up to five episodes by default, with deterministic lexical, action/tag, and recency ranking; it does not match paraphrases.

Scope boundaries differ by component. The desk relies on repository-local installation and has no principal filter in the reviewed CLI. The engine's audience filter treats missing fact scope as internal and drops unscoped episodes when an audience is supplied; its separate wrapper maps a host-provided principal to a fixed policy and rejects unknown principals. The context output still includes the working goal and scratchpad regardless of audience, and the engine itself warns that caller-chosen audience is not an authorization boundary.

Provenance fields include desk source locators and checked dates; engine episodes carry IDs, timestamps, action, outcome and tags, and facts may link known episode IDs. Engine facts begin asserted; verification requires evidence and a distinct tool or human verifier. These fields do not authenticate the named verifier or adjudicate the evidence text.

metrics.evidence: Desk lookup and engine episode-ranking code are inspectable, but answerability and abstention probes were not run.
Desk tombstones and engine supersession/time filters are code-visible; no current-versus-stale probe set was run.
Retirement paths retain values in journals, tombstones, or episodes; no post-retirement leakage probes were run.
An optional engine audience filter and principal wrapper are present, but no deployment or cross-scope probe was run; the desk has repository-local scope.

Text, TSV, JSON, and JSONL stores are visible; persistent bytes and per-item sizes were not measured.

limits.text: This is a selected source review at one verified commit. The repository is a kit to adapt; deployments may differ in hook wiring, storage, permissions, and host authentication. The examples, tests, runtime integrations, and benchmarks were not executed.

The desk relies on lexical matching and human curation. Source inspection does not establish that stored rows are reachable or useful in a given repository. The separate engine documents that atomic per-file replacement does not prevent concurrent read-modify-write races, its episodic ledger is unbounded, and it has no built-in decay or use stamps.

Engine scope enforcement assumes a trusted host principal provider. In the inspected context builder, the audience filter excludes unscoped episodes but the working goal and scratchpad remain included; callers must consider that path when placing restricted data. This is a code review observation, not a demonstrated isolation leak.

The README describes an experience in one office and says some usage counts were counted by hand while instrumentation was new. That project-authored account is not a measured result from this review and cannot establish general recall quality, safe deletion, correction quality, benchmark performance, or cost.

benchmark.text: Benchmark not run for this review. No Breadcrumbs runtime, tests, or benchmark workload was executed. The repository contains synthetic benchmark designs; the project metric definitions and fixture specify a comparison protocol, while the execution-status record is separate and is not attributed here as a Breadcrumbs result.
